summary.headline: Advit Jewels Q1 FY27 total income rose 37.35% YoY to INR35.40 crore, with PAT up 37.86% to INR8.19 crore and a 23.12% PAT margin.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR35.40 crore (up 37.35% YoY from about INR25.78 crore), EBITDA of INR11.72 crore (33.12% margin, up 33.02%) and PAT of INR8.19 crore (up 37.86%). Revenue mix in the quarter was about 78% B2B and 22% B2C, both linked to bridal demand. Management said the company is now debt-free and is holding unutilised IPO proceeds for working capital and expansion. The call focused on the planned Jaipur flagship, company-owned metro stores, a franchise model for Tier 2 and smaller cities, and new categories (pret and men's jewellery). Many answers were general, and no formal numeric guidance was given.

financial_highlights.change: B2C was ~20% per management elsewhere in call

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: About 78% of Q1 FY27 revenue per management; mostly ready-stock sales, with customisation done on request at the in-house manufacturing facility.

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: About 22% of Q1 FY27 revenue; management targets B2C rising toward 40-50% of mix over time while keeping B2B stable.

segments.name: New categories
segments.commentary: Pret (lightweight, Gen Z and millennial) and contemporary men's jewellery are being launched alongside core bridal/Kundan-Polki; no revenue contribution disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 or FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance given; management said numbers 'will be going up' and that it 'will not let the numbers go down'.
Jaipur flagship (~30,000 sq ft) targeted for completion by November 2026, subject to interior delays from rains.
Franchise protocols and model expected to be ready within about one month of the call.
Company-owned stores planned in metro cities; franchises in Tier 2 and smaller cities. Franchise partner funds inventory; ~INR6-8 crore inventory needed per franchise store.
Company-owned store inventory of about INR5 crore per store (excluding capex).
capex_capacity: Jaipur flagship: total investment about INR24-25 crore (BOQ ~INR25 crore); land already acquired and building ready, interior work in progress.
Balance IPO funds: management cited about INR52-57 crore unspent (answer unclear), held for expansion and partly used for new inventory.
Working capital may rise with retail expansion; management said current capital is sufficient, with further funding considered later if needed.
Plans to build luxury boutique stores in metro cities; a brand ambassador to be announced with the Jaipur store opening.
demand_pricing: Management said bridal demand is strong and that designer jewellery is spreading beyond HNI buyers.

Rising gold prices have pushed customers to keep budgets fixed; the company is responding with lighter-gold designs using more stones and polki (e.g. a INR20 lakh budget buys less gold but a better design).
Gold is hedged at order booking when advances are received; procurement is matched to sold stock.
Management cited its 105-year legacy, in-house manufacturing and innovation as its USP against rising competition.
Export priority is US and Middle East, with UK for exclusive art-led pieces; no export numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Have all IPO proceeds been utilised, or is any portion pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt fully repaid; the balance is held for expansion and some was used for inventory. Management gave a figure of about 52-57 crore (unclear on the call).

qa_highlights.question: Jaipur flagship investment and expected returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Total investment about INR24-25 crore. Management did not give a revenue threshold for returns and pointed to DRHP projections and the quarter's results.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 split between B2B and B2C?
qa_highlights.answer: About 78% B2B and 22% B2C, both linked to bridal demand.

qa_highlights.question: Store ownership model and franchise economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Metro cities will have company-owned stores and Tier 2 and smaller cities franchises. Franchise partners fund inventory, about INR6-8 crore per store. Franchise protocols are due in about one month.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 and FY28 and margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance. Management said numbers will rise, based on Q1 performance and the IPO roadshow response.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Jaipur flagship economically justified on its own revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the store will serve as a hub that rotates jewellery to other stores and showcases pieces to customers in other cities, so store-level economics should not be judged in isolation.

risks_watch: Jaipur flagship timing (November target) and cost overrun risk given interior delays; brand-ambassador spend not quantified.
Working capital intensity of retail expansion and inventory build (~INR5 crore per company store); management said more funding may be needed later.
Franchise model not yet finalised; quality control and inventory funding terms with partners are still open.
Gold price volatility on customer budgets and the shift to lighter-gold designs; margin impact not quantified.
Competition in designer/polki jewellery; B2C scaling will need higher marketing and brand spend.
Unused IPO proceeds figure was unclear on the call; reconcile with the use-of-proceeds disclosure.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on brand, bridal demand and Q1 performance. Evasive or vague on numbers: no guidance, unclear IPO fund figures, and the Jaipur store return question was deflected. Franchise terms were deferred to protocols due in about a month.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report a strong start to financial year '27 with continued momentum across our business.
So, we had around 78% of B2B in this Q1 as I have come to know, 22% we have done B2C and both the demands were connected to bridals.
We will not let the numbers go down anyway. Numbers will be going up as our first quarter you can see.
So, we have paid our debts. We are totally debt -free now as one of the portion was to be paid for our loans.

adds.what: Jaipur flagship store (~30,000 sq ft), capex ~INR24-25 crore

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management says numbers 'will be going up', with the Jaipur flagship targeted for November 2026 (about 2 quarters out, subject to interior delays) and franchise protocols due in about a month, backed by strong bridal demand and Q1 total income up 37.35% YoY.
